title: Feature Settings — AI tab
description: Master AI features card with per-product retention, plus AVA / Phone AI / Chat AI parent cards whose detail pages (deep-linkable via ?detail=) hold the dependent features and cascade rules.

designSystem.name: Spring UI (tokens + icons; components are Spring-styled Tailwind/Radix equivalents)

targets.title: AI tab — main list

hierarchy: SettingCard “AI features” (master) — switch, and while on: “AI data custom retention period” subsection with per-product summary pills (RingEX phone / Meetings / RingCX, 365 days each) and Manage
elements.layout: Stacked cards; parent cards show a right-aligned “N features” descriptor + CaretRight, vertically centered.
elements.styling: Icons from @ringcentral/spring-icon (AiStarsMd, AvaMd, CallMd, Ivamd) rendered 20px via SpringIcon wrapper with currentColor.

states.description: Three 120px-tall pulsing slate skeleton bars replace the panel for ~250ms after every tab activation (FeatureSettings.tsx).
All three parent cards are hidden; only the master card (switch off, no retention subsection) remains.

localInteractions.outcome: Navigates to /feature-settings/ai?detail=<ava|phoneAi|chatAi>; the detail page takes over the whole surface (page heading + pill tabs hidden).
Confirm dialog; turning off also cascades AVA off and returns to the main list.
A top-center toast (“Settings were updated.” or “<Feature> turned on/off”) appears with an Undo action that reverts the last snapshot.

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: persisting feature settings, error handling, and undo semantics
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: All changes mutate an in-memory reducer store; Undo restores a single snapshot; a simulateError flag fakes save failures.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Use the repository’s existing settings persistence, error handling, and undo/rollback approach.

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: real per-feature user override counts and org user totals
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: Counts such as “26/98 users” are mock constants seeded in the store.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Resolve counts from the production user-settings service.

integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: Retention values are numbers in mock state.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Bind to production retention policy services.

acceptance: Deep links to any ?detail= page redirect to the main list when master AI is off.
Parent cards disappear when master is off.

targets.title: AVA detail page
targets.description: Back-arrow detail page. AVA parent row (switch + summary + Manage) nests 5 dependent feature rows: Query, Messaging, Integrations, Actions, Knowledge Base — each with its own switch, summary pills, Manage.

hierarchy: 5 nested child rows (visible only while AVA is active)
elements.layout: Single card; children indented under the parent row.
elements.styling: Child config lives in local component state (not the store); defaults: on, User default On, access Allowed.

states.description: All 5 children visible with pills and Manage.

localInteractions.trigger: Save AVA Manage with User default Off
localInteractions.outcome: Cascade confirm “Turn off default for users?” listing the 5 children; confirming cascades default Off to every child.

localInteractions.trigger: Save AVA Manage with access Restricted
localInteractions.outcome: Cascade confirm “Restrict users from changing this setting?”; confirming restricts every child. Both confirms chain when both changes apply.
Turn-off confirm or enable dialog; commits to local state with toast (no Undo for children).

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: backing state for the 5 AVA dependent features
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: Children use local component state keyed by title; Undo of an AVA cascade restores a local snapshot.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Model these features in the production settings store.

actions: Click Manage on the AVA row
activationRecipe.expected: “Turn off default for users?” confirm listing Query, Messaging, Integrations, Actions, Knowledge Bases.

acceptance: Restrictive AVA changes always confirm the child cascade before committing.

targets.title: Phone AI detail page
targets.description: Three cards implementing the Closed captioning → Live transcripts → Call notes dependency chain, plus AI voicemail summaries. Every enabled feature shows User default and User access summaries with a Manage action.

hierarchy: Card 1: Closed captioning — switch, User default/User access pills, Manage
Card 2 (hidden while Closed captioning is off): Live transcripts row; nested Call notes row (hidden while Live transcripts is off); each enabled row has deployment pills and Manage
Card 2 shared row: standard divider + dynamic Automatic live transcripts [& call notes]: On/Off summary pill + Manage, or Locked status when policy is forced
Card 3: AI voicemail summaries — switch, User default/User access pills, Manage
elements.layout: Stacked established Feature Settings cards. Deployment summaries sit 8px below descriptions. The shared automatic behavior uses the existing divider, pill, and right-aligned action pattern.
elements.styling: Spring tokens and icons: ClosedCaptionsMd, TranscriptMd, SmartNotesMd, VoicemailMd. No feature-specific visual system.

states.description: All rows visible with deployment summaries. Shared row label is Automatic live transcripts & call notes.
Call notes remains visible with its switch off; its deployment summary hides. Shared row label changes to Automatic live transcripts.
Live transcripts/Call notes card hidden entirely.
Call notes row and shared automatic-behavior row hidden.
If an enabled affected feature has User default On and User access Restricted, automatic behavior is forced On; Manage is replaced by Locked and helper text.

localInteractions.trigger: Turn on Closed captioning, Call notes, or AI voicemail summaries
localInteractions.outcome: Opens the standard user-deployment confirmation with User default On/Off, User access Allowed/Restricted, and Reset/Restore choices when custom settings exist.

Opens the same user-deployment confirmation with an In-call behavior section containing the shared automatic setting; confirming saves deployment and automatic behavior atomically and also enables required Closed captioning.

localInteractions.trigger: Click Manage for an enabled Phone AI feature
localInteractions.outcome: Opens the established user-deployment dialog; Save is disabled until changed.

localInteractions.trigger: Turn off any Phone AI feature
localInteractions.outcome: The confirmation says the feature will be unavailable to users and that previous user settings can be restored when turned back on; dependency warnings name only enabled features that will also turn off.
Opens the standard Manage modal; the dynamic setting label reflects whether Call notes is enabled, and Save is disabled until changed.

localInteractions.trigger: Save an affected feature as User default On + User access Restricted
localInteractions.outcome: The shared automatic behavior becomes On. Manage remains visible but disabled, and an adjacent info icon reveals the restriction reason on hover or keyboard focus.

localInteractions.trigger: Save a deployment change that newly forces automatic behavior On
localInteractions.outcome: Before committing, opens a confirmation explaining that Automatic live transcripts or Automatic live transcripts & call notes will also turn on because users are restricted. Cancel preserves the previous state; Confirm commits the deployment, parent-default cascade, and effective automatic behavior atomically.

acceptance: Every enabled Phone AI feature shows User default and User access pills plus Manage.
Deployment summaries sit exactly 8px below feature descriptions.
Closed captioning off hides the Live transcripts/Call notes card; Live transcripts off hides Call notes and the shared row.
The shared label is Automatic live transcripts when Call notes is off and Automatic live transcripts & call notes when it is on.
Only an enabled affected feature with default On and Restricted access forces the shared behavior On and locked.
All four turn-on flows include user-deployment management; Live transcripts includes shared automatic behavior in that same confirmation.
Every Phone AI turn-off confirm includes: When turned back on, previous user settings can be restored.
Dependency warnings mention only currently enabled features that will also turn off.
In-call behavior appears inline before the automatic-setting pill on the enabled settings page; the turn-on dialog keeps the section label above its container.
A deployment change that newly forces automatic behavior On requires explicit confirmation with a label derived from the post-confirmation Call notes state.

targets.title: Chat AI detail page
targets.description: Four independent cards: AI writer for messaging, AI summary, AI translation, AI writer for SMS — each with switch, summary pills, Manage, standard enable/disable dialogs.

localInteractions.outcome: PATCH_AI_FEATURE + undo toast; no cross-feature cascades on this page.

Three product rows with day selectors.
Shown only when a value decreases.

activationRecipe.expected: Data-loss confirm dialog opens; only after confirming does the change commit.

flows.title: Main list ↔ detail pages

acceptedDeviations.requirement: Keep the prototype’s Spring-styled Tailwind + Radix primitives (SettingCard, SpringSwitch, SpringConfirmDialog, etc.); @ringcentral/spring-ui is not installed and the task forbids redesigning the finalized UI.
Keep lucide-react utility glyphs (close X, chevrons, search, info) inside dialogs/controls; visual parity with the approved prototype takes precedence.
Keep Tailwind default-palette utilities used for the loading skeleton (slate-100), error banners (red-50/red-800), overlays (black/40) and white surfaces.
Admin Portal chrome (masthead, side nav, footer) intentionally uses the legacy Service Web UI palette (#0679BA, #2F2F2F, #FBFBFB…) scoped under .swui-scope, not Spring tokens.
Keep the inline checkmark SVG inside the shared automatic-behavior checkbox used by the Live transcripts enable and Manage dialogs (visual parity with the approved dialog).

sourceClosureNote: The app is a single SPA: src/App.tsx statically imports FeatureSettings.tsx, which statically imports all five tab panels and the AI helper modules. sourceFiles therefore lists the full transitive import graph — identical for every feature — so any manifest alone is a complete, buildable source set. Files primary to this feature carry feature-specific descriptions; the rest are marked (shared closure).
